university: The University of Texas at Tyler

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Language for Syllabi
tiers: AI is permitted only for specific assignments, with acknowledgement
AI is not permitted at all
documents.summary: Academic Affairs requires every UT Tyler syllabus to carry common AI language and one of three instructor-chosen categories (encouraged, permitted for specific assignments, not permitted), with sample statements for each. The common language requires acknowledgement of AI use, bars protected or copyrighted data, and sends misuse to the Academic Integrity Policy.
documents.stance_why: The page says "All UT Tyler faculty must identify to what degree students may utilize artificial intelligence (AI) tools" and offers "three basic categories" with sample statements, so the university sets no single stance and hands the choice to instructors, with templates listed in tiers.

units.anchor: All UT Tyler faculty must identify to what degree students may utilize artificial intelligence

units.why: "There are three basic categories for using AI tools" defines named categories of use, which is P05; it is a description of the framework, so informs.
units.anchor: There are three basic categories for using AI tools
units.policy: The university offers three basic categories of AI use, with example statements for each

documents.title: AI Guidelines & Policies
documents.summary: Digital Learning guidance names the Microsoft tools UT Tyler licenses, limits what data may go into ChatGPT-type tools, and lists prohibited uses such as grading and decisions about people. It also points to policy, copyright and click-through-contract risks and repeats the duty to state a course AI rule.
documents.stance_why: The page says "All UT Tyler faculty must specify the extent to which students are permitted to use" AI tools, and its own rules concern data, tools and legal use rather than a student-work stance, so the decision on coursework is delegated to instructors.

units.why: "Responsible AI use starts with clear guidelines and a shared commitment to ethical practice" states the purpose and principle of the guidelines, P56.
units.anchor: Responsible AI use starts with clear guidelines and a shared commitment to ethical practice.

units.why: "All UT Tyler faculty must specify the extent to which students are permitted to use" AI tools requires an AI statement in each course, P09.
units.anchor: All UT Tyler faculty must specify the extent to which students are permitted to use

units.why: "Microsoft Copilot ... and Azure Open AI (AOAI) are available AI tools with contractual agreements for use by UT Tyler" names the university-approved tools, P92.
units.anchor: are available AI tools with contractual agreements for use by UT Tyler

units.why: "we highly recommend against using Bing Copilot on sensitive data sets" advises against sensitive data in a vetted tool, P50.
units.anchor: we highly recommend against using Bing Copilot on sensitive data sets

units.why: "use of Microsoft AI tools should be consistent with the Information Resources Acceptable Use Policy" requires compliance with existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: use of Microsoft AI tools should be consistent with the

units.why: "We highly encourage use of the Microsoft products specified above exclusively to fulfill official University duties" prefers the licensed tools, P92.
units.anchor: We highly encourage use of the Microsoft products specified above exclusively

units.why: "Only data that is publicly available or defined as Published Data ... can be used freely in AI Tools" limits what data enters ChatGPT-type tools, P50.
units.anchor: Only data that is publicly available or defined as Published Data

units.why: "Students should always adhere to the UT Tyler Policy on Student Conduct when using any AI tool" ties student AI use to existing conduct rules, P77.
units.anchor: Students should always adhere to the

units.why: "Researchers should always adhere to the UT Tyler Policy 3.2.8 Misconduct in Research and Other Scholarly Activity" governs AI in research, P62.
units.anchor: Researchers should always adhere to the UT Tyler Policy

units.why: "any use of ChatGPT or similar AI Tools cannot include any personal, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information" bans sensitive data in AI, P50.
units.anchor: cannot include any personal, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information

units.why: "student records subject to FERPA, health information (HIPAA), proprietary information ... must not be used with ChatGPT or similar AI Tools" names protected data classes, P50.
units.anchor: student records subject to FERPA, health information (HIPAA), proprietary information

units.why: "must not be used to generate output that would not be considered authorized" limits AI output by copyright and fair use, P52.
units.anchor: must not be used to generate output that would not be considered authorized

units.why: "generating someone else’s proprietary or unpublished research" is a listed prohibited example, P52.
units.anchor: generating someone else’s proprietary or unpublished research

units.why: "recruitment, personnel or disciplinary decision making" lists decisions about people AI must not be used for, P73.
units.anchor: recruitment, personnel or disciplinary decision making

units.why: "completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor" prohibits AI work the instructor has not permitted; P04 because the instructor sets what is allowed, and P19 does not fit since it bans all generation.
units.anchor: completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor

units.why: "creation of someone else’s proprietary instructional materials without authorized use or proper citations" is a listed prohibited use, P52.
units.anchor: creation of someone else’s proprietary instructional materials without authorized use or proper citations

units.why: "and grading" is listed among uses AI must not be used for, so P46 (humans assign grades).
units.anchor: instructional materials without authorized use or proper citations; and grading

units.why: "OpenAI and Microsoft ... explicitly forbid their use for certain categories of activity, including fraud and illegal activities" notes vendor terms, P77.
units.anchor: explicitly forbid their use for certain categories of activity, including fraud and illegal activities
units.fit_note: Refers to vendor terms of use as well as law and university policy.

units.why: "AI Tools of any sort may not be used for any activity that would be illegal, fraudulent or a violation of any state or federal law" requires legal compliance; P77 fits and P74 does not name deception generally.
units.anchor: may not be used for any activity that would be illegal, fraudulent or a violation

units.why: "Fair use is a legal doctrine that promotes freedom of expression" defines fair use, so P52, informs.
units.anchor: Fair use is a legal doctrine that promotes freedom of expression

units.why: "Users should not enter any Confidential or Controlled university data in an AI chat tool" protects university data, P50.
units.anchor: Users should not enter any Confidential or Controlled university data in an AI chat

units.why: "Users should always validate the results and verify the sources of information provided by AI tools" requires checking AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Users should always validate the results and verify the sources of information provided

units.why: "Users should not violate any policies, including the UT Tyler Information Resources Acceptable Use Policy and the specific policies of each AI tool" requires policy compliance, P77.
units.anchor: Users should not violate any policies, including the UT Tyler

units.why: "please contact the Information Security Office" names the office that answers questions on appropriate use, P80.
units.anchor: please contact the Information Security Office
units.fit_note: Names a contact for questions, not an enforcement or exception body.

units.why: "All content entered into with, or generated by, ChatGPT is available to ChatGPT, its parent company, OpenAI" warns that prompts are stored by the vendor, P50.
units.anchor: All content entered into with, or generated by, ChatGPT is available to ChatGPT

units.why: "There is currently no agreement between UT Tyler and OpenAI ... that would provide data security and privacy protections" explains why unvetted tools are risky, P50.
units.anchor: There is currently no agreement between UT Tyler and OpenAI or other AI Tools

units.why: "Individuals who accept click-through agreements without delegated signature authority may face personal consequences" warns about terms-of-use liability, P52.
units.anchor: Individuals who accept click-through agreements without delegated signature authority may face personal consequences

units.why: "Violation of any UT Tyler policies may result in disciplinary action that may include termination ... suspension or expulsion in the case of a student" states penalties by role; P37 is nearest.
units.anchor: Violation of any UT Tyler policies may result in disciplinary action that may include termination
units.fit_note: Penalties apply to policy violations generally, not AI misuse specifically.

notes: No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred. Both documents are university-wide and delegate course-level decisions to instructors.
